editorial:
Imagine being a therapist who is supposed to have all the answers, only to have a ten-year-old kid tell you that he is actually the one in charge. That is exactly what happens here. You follow a woman who thinks she is helping a young boy, but he starts predicting things about her life that should be impossible to know. The vibe is very creepy and makes you wonder if the kid is actually psychic or if the therapist is just losing her mind. It is a slow-burn kind of story that keeps you guessing about who is really playing whom.

The acting is great, especially the kid, who is naturally scary without even trying. You might find the pacing a bit slow at first, but the twists make it worth the wait. If you enjoy psychological games, you will love this.
endingExplained: At the end, you find out that the boy was not actually magic. He was just very smart and used psychological tricks to manipulate the therapist. He figured out her weaknesses and played her like a puppet. The twist is that she completely broke down and believed he had power over her future. It ends with her totally lost in her own head, proving that the boy won the game he started.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves mind games and surprising twists.
